title: Best Time to See Rhino and Tiger in Chitwan
meta_description: When to visit Chitwan for rhino and tiger: a month-by-month guide to grass height, heat, monsoon and fog, and why February to April gives the best sightings.
summary: February to April is the best time to see wildlife in Chitwan. The tall grass has been cut and burnt, water is scarce and animals gather by rivers and lakes. Rhino can be seen all year; tigers are rare at any time but most often seen in the hot, dry months of March to May.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: If you want the best chance of rhino and a real, if small, chance of tiger, come between February and April. By then the elephant grass that covers much of the park has been cut by villagers and burnt back by park staff, new green shoots draw grazing animals into the open, and as the dry season advances, rivers and lakes become the only places to drink. Visibility is the best of the year and the weather is still bearable, with warm days and cool mornings.

October to January is also a good time to visit, with comfortable temperatures and clear skies, but the grass is at its tallest and sightings depend more on the river and open areas. May is very hot, often 38 °C or more, and the monsoon, June to September, brings rain, leeches and closed tracks. Rhino, however, are seen in every month; it is the rarer animals that follow the seasons.

sections.heading: Why grass decides everything
paras: About a fifth of Chitwan is grassland, and much of it is tall grass that grows several metres high after the monsoon, taller than a jeep and thick enough to hide an elephant. From October to January a rhino can stand a few metres from the track and you will only hear it. That is the single biggest factor in sightings.

For a few days each winter, usually in January or February, the park opens to people from the buffer zone villages to cut thatch grass for roofs, ropes and mats. It is a tradition that keeps local communities connected to the park. Park staff then burn patches of old grass, which allows fresh growth. Within weeks the grassland is short, green and full of grazing animals: rhino, chital, hog deer and the occasional gaur. Visibility stays good until the monsoon.

sections.heading: Month by month in Chitwan
paras: This table summarises what each month is like on safari. Temperatures are typical daytime highs and dawn lows around Sauraha; individual years vary, and recent years have brought hotter springs and more erratic monsoons.

sections.heading: The best time for rhino
paras: The one-horned rhino is the animal almost every visitor sees. Chitwan held 694 of Nepal's 752 rhino in the 2021 count, many of them in the grassland and riverine forest close to Sauraha and Meghauli. They feed in the grass in the mornings and evenings, wallow in pools and rivers in the heat and often cross the Rapti to graze in the buffer zone, sometimes in full view of the tea stalls of Sauraha.

In the dry months, from February to May, rhino spend long hours in the water, which makes them easy to find from a canoe or the riverbank. In winter they are just as present but harder to see in the tall grass; look for them at the river edge and in the open floodplain. Even in the monsoon, rhino are often seen from the village side of the river.

sections.heading: The best time for tiger
paras: Nepal's 2022 national survey estimated about 128 tigers in Chitwan, one of the highest numbers for any single park in the country. Still, tigers are shy, mostly active at dawn, dusk and night, and travel long distances. Most visitors never see one. The best chances come from March to May, when the grass is short and water is scarce, and tigers come to drink or rest in the shade of riverbanks.

Full-day jeep safaris that go deep into the park, away from busy tracks near Sauraha, improve the odds. So does spending more days. Experienced naturalists listen for the alarm calls of chital, sambar and langur, which often warn of a predator moving. Even if you do not see a tiger, fresh pugmarks in the sand and a sudden chorus of alarm calls are thrilling in their own right.

If a tiger is your main goal, consider adding Bardia National Park in the far west, which had about 125 tigers in 2022 and far fewer visitors. Many naturalists rate it the better park for tiger sightings, though Chitwan wins on rhino and variety.

sections.heading: Other wildlife through the year
paras: Birds follow their own calendar. From November to March, winter visitors such as ducks, waders, raptors and some songbirds arrive from the north, and the lakes and rivers fill with life. From March to May resident birds breed and sing, and colourful summer visitors like the Indian pitta arrive. Sloth bear and gaur are seen most often in the dry season, when the grass is short. Gharial and mugger crocodile are easiest to see basking on sandbanks on sunny winter and spring days.
list: Sloth bear: February to May, in grassland and forest edges
Gaur: dry season, near the Churia hills and forest clearings
Leopard: any time, rare, often at forest edges
Gharial: winter and spring sunshine on river sandbanks
Winter birds: November to March, especially on lakes and the Narayani

sections.heading: Planning around heat, fog and festivals
paras: December and January bring thick fog to the Terai on many mornings, which can delay flights into Bharatpur by an hour or more and keeps early safaris cold and grey until mid-morning. The fog also gives beautiful, misty light for photography. From April, plan safaris for early morning and late afternoon and rest in the middle of the day, when temperatures can pass 35 °C.

October and November coincide with Dashain and Tihar, Nepal's biggest festivals, when domestic travel peaks and hotels fill. Book early in these months and from February to April. Monsoon travel, from June to September, is possible for keen travellers on a budget, but expect heavy rain, high rivers, leeches and limited activities; some lodges close or scale down. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: What to pack for each season
paras: Chitwan's seasons ask for different kit, and the right clothes make early safaris far more comfortable. Winter mornings in an open jeep are much colder than the daytime temperature suggests, while spring afternoons are hot enough to make long sleeves feel heavy. Whatever the month, choose neutral colours: green, khaki, brown or grey. White shows up across the grassland, and bright colours seem to make animals more wary.

Pack light and layer. Most lodges offer laundry, and Sauraha has small shops for sun hats, ponchos and repellent if you forget something. Binoculars matter more than a long lens for most people; even a basic 8x42 pair turns a distant brown shape into a rhino with a calf.
list: December to January: fleece, windproof jacket, warm hat and gloves for dawn jeeps; light layers for afternoon
February to March: a light fleece for mornings, long light trousers and shirts for the day
April to May: breathable long sleeves against sun and insects, a wide hat, electrolyte sachets and a refillable bottle
June to September: rain jacket or poncho, quick-dry clothes, leech socks and a dry bag for cameras
October to November: light layers, insect repellent for evenings, sunscreen for midday on the river

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Chitwan?
faqs.a: February and March are the best months for most travellers. The grass has been cut and burnt, visibility is excellent, rhino and deer graze in the open, and temperatures are warm without being extreme. April is also excellent for wildlife but hotter. October and November are pleasant for weather, though the grass is still tall.

faqs.q: Can I see rhino in Chitwan all year?
faqs.a: Yes. One-horned rhino are seen in every month, often from the riverbank in Sauraha or from a canoe on the Rapti. Chitwan held 694 rhino in the 2021 count. In the tall-grass months of October to January they are harder to spot from a jeep, but the river and open floodplains still give good chances.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see a tiger in Chitwan?
faqs.a: March to May, when the grass is short, water is scarce and tigers come to rivers and pools. Even then sightings are rare; most visitors see pugmarks, not tigers. Full-day jeep safaris deep into the park and more days in the park improve your chances. For better odds, add Bardia National Park.

faqs.q: Is Chitwan worth visiting in the monsoon?
faqs.a: For keen travellers on a budget, sometimes. From June to September the jungle is green and lush and crowds disappear, but heavy rain closes many tracks, rivers run high and canoe trips may stop. Leeches and humidity are constant. Rhino can still be seen near Sauraha, but expect limited activities and some lodges closed.

From April to June daytime highs often reach 35 to 40 °C, with high humidity before the monsoon. Winters are mild, with highs of 22 to 25 °C and dawn temperatures of 7 to 9 °C. Safaris in hot months run early and late in the day, with a long rest at midday.

faqs.q: Why is the grass in Chitwan so tall in autumn?
faqs.a: After the monsoon, the park's grasslands grow several metres high, taller than a jeep. This tall grass is vital habitat for rhino, deer and tigers, but it hides animals from view. In winter, buffer zone villagers are allowed in for a few days to cut thatch, and park staff burn patches, which brings fresh, short growth by February.

faqs.q: Is December a good time for Chitwan?
faqs.a: Yes, with caveats. December has dry, sunny afternoons and few mosquitoes, but mornings are often foggy and cold, around 7 to 10 °C, and flights can be delayed. The grass is still tall, so jeep sightings are harder than in spring. Canoe trips and riverbank walks work well, and the misty light is lovely for photography.

faqs.q: When do migratory birds arrive in Chitwan?
faqs.a: Winter visitors arrive from November and stay until about March, filling the lakes and rivers with ducks, waders and raptors. Summer visitors such as the Indian pitta arrive around April and May for the breeding season. For the widest variety of species, February and March combine late winter visitors with early breeders.

faqs.q: Are Chitwan safaris crowded in peak season?
faqs.a: Around Sauraha, yes, at times. October, November and February to April see many jeeps and canoes on the eastern tracks. Full-day safaris deep into the park, or staying at Meghauli or Amaltari in the west, avoid most of the crowds. Early starts also help, as many jeeps leave after breakfast.
